## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Skate Hire
where: ReportService (uses), src/business/reportService.ts, component business
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
for (const [size, qty] of Object.entries(b.hire)) {
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B
concept: Hire Skate Stock
where: HireStockRepository (defines), src/persistence/hireStockRepository.ts, component persistence

private readonly stock = new Map<string, number>();
=====SOURCE-END=====
graph:

- <- CALLS Method RinkService.getHireStock
- <- CALLS Method RinkService.purchase

response.rationale: A ('Skate Hire') is the per-booking hire request: ReportService iterates `Object.entries(b.hire)` (src/business/reportService.ts) to read size→quantity hired on a booking. B ('Hire Skate Stock') is the rink's inventory of hire skates: HireStockRepository holds `private readonly stock = new Map<string, number>()` (src/persistence/hireStockRepository.ts), managed by RinkService via getHireStock/setHireStock/getAvailability/purchase. Both are keyed by size, but one is demand recorded on a booking line and the other is available supply. They are related (availability = stock minus hires), not the same concept.
